profile.summary: PlantRNA-FM is an RNA language model for plants. It was pretrained on transcript sequences from 1,124 plant species, together with predicted secondary structure and labels for the 5' UTR, coding sequence and 3' UTR. It reads an RNA sequence one nucleotide at a time and outputs per-nucleotide embeddings, which the authors fine-tune for tasks such as genic region annotation and translation efficiency, and use to find RNA sequence and structure motifs linked to translation.

summary_quotes.text: PlantRNA-FM was pretrained on an extensive dataset, integrating RNA sequences and RNA structure information from 1,124 distinct plant species.
In addition, we incorporated RNA annotation information (CDS and UTRs)
We leveraged the single-nucleotide tokenization method within PlantRNA-FM
PlantRNA-FM achieves an F1 score of 0.974 for genic region annotation
we developed an interpretable framework for our PlantRNA-FM to explore the RNA features within the 5′ UTR that influences translation

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: PlantRNA-FM is an encoder-only transformer with 12 layers and an embedding dimension of 480. Each nucleotide is one token, and positions are encoded with rotary position embedding. Pretraining used three objectives together: masked nucleotide modelling, in which 20% of nucleotides in each sequence are selected for masking and reconstructed; prediction of the RNA secondary structure, which the authors annotated with ViennaRNA (RNAfold); and classification of each nucleotide into CDS, 5' UTR or 3' UTR. For a downstream task the authors replace the output layer and fine-tune the model. To find motifs, they use the model's attention contrast matrix with unsupervised hierarchical clustering.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: One checkpoint is published, yangheng/PlantRNA-FM on Hugging Face; this page read it at revision 5e7baf4e. The model card points users to a newer model from the same group, OmniGenome-186M, also trained on OneKP; it is a separate model and not described here. The sources disagree on some details. The paper and model card describe 24 attention heads, while the published config.json sets 20. The GitHub README says the model handles up to 512 nucleotides, while the paper says pretraining used 512 and fine-tuning allowed up to 1,026 tokens, the model card says up to 1026 nucleotides, and config.json sets max_position_embeddings to 1026. A result should name the Hugging Face revision. The GitHub repository holds the fine-tuning datasets and task scripts; the paper says training and inference code is in the Hugging Face repository.

run_guide.summary: Install the listed Python packages, download the PlantRNA-FM weights from Hugging Face and print per-nucleotide embeddings for the README's example RNA sequence.
prerequisites: Python 3.9+, PyTorch 2.0+, Transformers 4.38+ and pytorch-cuda 11.0+ (conda), as listed in the README.
The authors say the model fits a consumer GPU such as an RTX 4090 at batch size 16; the sources do not state a minimum.
Weights and code are MIT licensed; the weights are not gated.

steps.title: Load the model and embed a sequence
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer

model_name_or_path = "yangheng/PlantRNA-FM"

model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name_or_path)
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name_or_path)

rna_sequence = 'GCCGACUUAGCUCAGU<mask>GGGAGAGCGUUAGACUGAAGAUCUAAAGGUCCCUGGUUCGAUCCCGGGAGUCGGCACCA'

inputs = tokenizer(rna_sequence, return_tensors="pt")
outputs = model(**inputs)
print(outputs.last_hidden_state)
PY
steps.explanation: The README's Model loading and Inference snippets joined and wrapped in a shell heredoc. The first run downloads the weights from Hugging Face.
